terms.definition: What it is not: A single status What it actually means: A filter lane containing three statuses: cooling + ready + snoozed. It excludes bought and skipped.

What it is not: The whole 14-day process What it actually means: One status: the decision date is still in the future, so Buy is disabled. A snoozed wish also has a countdown but is not counted as cooling.
What it is not: "The AI approved it" What it actually means: The clock has run out. The verdict may still say skip, wait, or sample first. Ready only means the Buy button is unlocked.

What it is not: A lock or a ban What it actually means: The amber/rose verdict tone for SKIP_DUPLICATE ("blocked as duplicate"). Buy can still be enabled if the wish is ready. It is unrelated to Locked, which is the disabled Buy button during cooling, or BOT-BLOCKED, which is a library website refusing automated checks.

What it is not: A stored status What it actually means: Deck copy uses "cleared" to mean an approved verdict. Gate copy uses "gate cleared" to mean the 14-day clock finished. They are different things.

Context: A product page Meaning there: The archived title, price, and source excerpt captured at promotion or ingest (snapshot_excerpt, snapshot_status). Context: Data & Backups Meaning there: A timestamped copy of the vault, used to undo an import.

Context: Library Meaning there: The link-health check that produced LIVE/BOT-BLOCKED/NEEDS REVIEW and removed confirmed-dead links. Context: A wish Meaning there: The one-item oracle read, or the 1M-context vault synthesis. Neither changes the wish automatically.
Context: A wish Meaning there: best_source is the store/discounter; source_platform on a protocol is where the routine came from; a ledger entry's source is where the purchase happened.
Context: Library Meaning there: The site answered the audit. Context: Top bar Meaning there: NEBIUS LIVE means an API key is configured, not that a request is in flight.
Context: Gate Meaning there: Bought or skipped, still reopenable. Context: Library Meaning there: Hidden from active counts, still recoverable from the Archived filter.
Also called: Command deck, dashboard What lives there: Counts, budget envelope, verdict mix, last digest, router feed.
Also called: Signal index, memory What lives there: All saved links, 14 clusters, semantic search, cluster covers.
Also called: Reference library What lives there: The non-shopping subset of saved links, filed on 10 shelves with a description and a "use for" note.
Also called: Impulse gate, wishlist What lives there: Wishes under a cooling-off clock, verdicts, budget and the spend ledger.
Also called: Protocols, playbooks What lives there: Pasted routines turned into structured, checkable protocols.
Also called: Identity buffer, personal context What lives there: Owner, location, sizes, hard constraints, owned inventory, scent profile, default cooling period.
Also called: Ingest studio What lives there: URL, screenshot-text, or note intake that classifies a signal and can start a gate item.
Also called: Token Factory router What lives there: Model routing, the 1M-context oracle, telemetry, and the serverless digest job.

Any saved link: a browser bookmark, a social/product link pasted into Capture, or a promotion candidate. The Deck's Signals indexed count is the total number of signals (total_bookmarks, 1,346 in the seed).

The whole private dataset, not just the links. It contains bookmarks, wishlist, protocols, personal_context, spending_ledger, routine_log, telemetry, last_digest, and metadata. In a local install it is data/vault.json; on Vercel it is the private Blob object state/vault.json.

A signal with a URL, title, domain, browser, original folder, category, subcategory, tags, snapshot status, and embedding. Product links and reference links share the same bookmark record; the Library classification decides which room they appear in.

One of 14 top-level categories used to browse the Vault. The seeded clusters are Programming & Cloud, Life Hacks & Utilities, AI & Infrastructure, Career & Interview Prep, Menswear & Streetwear, Business/Finance/Auto/Real Estate, Watches/Footwear/Accessories, Gaming & Esports, Soccer Kits, Skincare & Health, Global Sourcing, Fragrances, Cybersecurity, and Food/Halal.

The image on a cluster card. It can be a live wishlist product photo or a generated reference card. Hero wishlist item is the wish whose photo supplies the cover; "auto" picks the strongest verdict in that cluster.
A generated 800×600 SVG that represents a cluster when no product photo is appropriate. There is one for each cluster in public/cluster-cards/.
The Deck card showing total signals, the four largest clusters, and which browser profiles were synced.
The Deck ring showing remaining fun-money, spent, and the monthly cap.

The Vault search label. It is lexical matching across title, domain, description, use-for, category, and tags, with a local vector tie-breaker; it does not call an LLM. Library search is a simpler all-words substring match over the same fields.
A potential-savings figure: for every wish, retail price − best verified floor, summed. It includes wishes you have not bought, so treat it as money identified, not money saved.

The report written by the most recent Nebius serverless job run (not necessarily last night): links verified, wishes polled, timers cleared, budget left, and the largest price drops. Stored as last_digest; also mirrored on the Router tab.
The most recent telemetry rows shown on the Deck. It is a log of model work, not a social feed.
A reviewed product saved into the Gate. A wish is created by the pre-gate review (from a bookmark, a pasted link, or Capture), never silently by saving a bookmark.
The stored wishlist array. The Gate is its UI; a wishlist item and a Gate item are the same record.

Both the room and the rule set. The room shows wishes, verdicts, budget, and the ledger. The rule set enforces the cooling-off clock, the owned-inventory check, the price floor, the budget, and routine conflicts.
Another name for a wish.

What it means: The decision date is in the future. The card shows COOLING OFF — n days left. Buy?: Disabled Counted in: Active / Cooling Only cooling. A snoozed wish is not in this lane even though it also has a countdown.
What it means: The decision date has arrived. The card says Ready — gate cleared. Buy?: Enabled Counted in: Active / Ready Only ready.
What it means: The decision date was deliberately pushed out. The card shows SNOOZED — n days left. Buy?: Disabled Counted in: Active / Snoozed Only snoozed.
What it means: A purchase was recorded. One ledger entry is written. The card moves to History. Buy?: n/a Counted in: History
What it means: The wish was archived without spending. No ledger entry. The card moves to History. Buy?: n/a Counted in: History
Cooling + ready + snoozed. This is the default Gate lane. "Items gated" on the Deck uses this number.
Bought + skipped. This is where decisions go after they are made.
When the wish entered the Gate. This is when the clock starts — not when the bookmark was first saved.
added_at plus the cooling period. The decision cannot be bought before this timestamp.
The length stored on that wish. The default is 14, configured by personal_context.default_cooling_off_days. Existing wishes keep their own value; changing the default only affects new wishes.
Whole days remaining until the later of unlock_at and snoozed_until, rounded up. It is 0 for bought and skipped wishes.
The new decision date after a Snooze.
When the decision was recorded.
The default rule: a new wish cannot be bought for 14 days. The length is per wish, so a legacy or manually created wish can differ.
UI language for "the Buy button is disabled." The button reads Locked Nd. It is not a stored status and not a verdict.
The UI note on a ready card. It means the clock finished, not that the purchase was approved.

Available only when the status is ready. Records the amount, source, and optional note in the spend ledger, sets purchased_at, and moves the wish to History. If the wish has no captured price, you must enter what you paid.
Archives the wish without spending. Allowed while cooling, ready, or snoozed. Sets skipped_at; no ledger entry. A skipped wish can be reopened.

Pushes the decision date out. The API accepts 1–90 days; the UI offers 7, 14, or 30. It extends from the latest of today, the original unlock date, and any previous snooze, so snoozing can never shorten an existing wait. It does not touch the ledger.

Returns a bought or skipped wish to the Gate. A bought wish's active ledger entries are voided automatically and the spend is removed from the month. If the original clock had already finished, the wish returns as ready immediately; reopening does not restart a fresh 14 days.

Corrects a mistaken ledger entry without deleting it. The entry stays in the file with voided: true, voided_at, and a reason; it is excluded from all totals. If it was linked to a bought wish and no other active purchase exists, the wish is reopened.
UI tone: Green Filter label: Approved Meaning: High-utility purchase that fills a real gap; the card gives the reason.
UI tone: Green Filter label: Approved Meaning: Approved, but buy from the named discounter/floor rather than retail.
UI tone: Amber Filter label: Cooling Meaning: Wait, sample first, consolidate duplicates, wait for a milestone, or resolve a routine conflict.
UI tone: Rose Filter label: Blocked Meaning: Skip because it duplicates something owned, overlaps too much, or is blocked by budget/label logic.

The human sentence on the card, stored as verdict_label. It is free text, so it can say "APPROVED — HIGH UTILITY GAP FILLER", "HOLD — ROUTINE CONFLICT", "BUDGET BLOCK …", or "PRICE NEEDS REVIEW". The filter uses the underlying code, not the label. A card labelled "BUDGET BLOCK" can therefore appear under Blocked because its code is SKIP_DUPLICATE.
A label used when a wish has no usable price. It does not mean the purchase is approved or rejected; the underlying verdict remains WAIT_OR_DUPE. Add a price in Details to clear it.
Promotion starts every wish as WAIT_OR_DUPE with the label 14-DAY COOLING LOCK ACTIVE, or PRICE NEEDS REVIEW when no price was confirmed.

Ingest can set SKIP_DUPLICATE for outerwear that matches owned hoodies/parkas, and WAIT_OR_DUPE for acid products that conflict with the evening retinoid. These are labels and recommendations; the clock still applies.
The verdict legend's "n cleared" counts green (BUY_RECOMMENDED + BUY_AT_DISCOUNTER) verdicts, not ready wishes.

The card header says THIS MONTH, but the counts run over the current wishlist, not a calendar-month filter. The three tones are green (approved), amber (wait/sample), and rose (blocked). The note's "n cleared" is the green count.
The reference/list price. Used as the top of the price rail and the anchor for savings.
The price the Gate expects you to pay, ideally from a discounter or verified source. This is the number used in the price block, budget preview, and savings calculation.
captured (read from page metadata or visible page text), manual (entered or corrected by you), or missing (no usable price; never replaced with a fake placeholder).
The small bar under the price block: the full width is retail, the filled part is the floor. It is a visual comparison, not a discount guarantee.

low means the number came from visible page text rather than structured metadata. The card labels it LOW-CONFIDENCE PAGE PRICE and asks you to verify before checkout. High/blank means captured or manual without that warning.
Where the number came from: page metadata, the browser bookmarklet, a manual edit, or a saved discounter. Shown as best_source on the card.
The card's SAVE $x badge: retail minus floor. If the numbers are equal it reads AT THE FLOOR; a low-confidence read reads VERIFY PRICE.
An optional price you set in Details. When the captured floor is at or below it, the card shows TARGET MET and the Gate summary lists a target hit.
Timestamped observations, capped at 60. Captures, manual edits, and Check price append to it. Repeating the same price within an hour updates the timestamp instead of adding a duplicate point.
The lowest price in the observation history, with lowest_seen_at. This is historical, not necessarily the current floor.
Re-reads the saved product page, records a new observation, updates the floor, and reports the change. Rate limited.
A rough unit economics estimate stored on the wish; editing prices recalculates it as floor ÷ uses_per_month.
The card's suggested equivalent or cheaper route. It is a recommendation, not a matched SKU.
The Owned check: whether the wish duplicates something in personal_context.owned_inventory. HIGH, DUPLICATE, or OVERLAP tones the row as a warning.
The Routine check: whether the product conflicts with your hard constraints or active protocol. CONFLICT, WARNING, or BLOCK tones the row as a warning.
The blunt paragraph under the checks explaining the verdict, the price provenance, or the main reason to wait.
The monthly discretionary budget. The seed cap is $300.
personal_context.monthly_discretionary_budget. Editable from Gate → Spend ledger → Edit budget. Defaults to $300 if unset.
The sum of active (non-voided) ledger entries for the current month. Remaining is cap minus spent. Over budget means remaining is negative.
Spend is keyed by month (YYYY-MM). On the first of a new month, the old entries no longer count against the cap; the cap itself does not reset. "Spent this month" is always derived from the ledger.
One auditable purchase row: id, linked item_id, title, category, amount, currency, spent_at, month, source, note, voided, created_at. A Buy writes exactly one entry.

The one-time migration row created from an older spent_this_month value when the ledger was introduced. In the seed it is $85, labelled "Existing spend (opening balance)". It is not a purchase and has no item link.
An entry kept for audit but excluded from totals. Voiding does not delete the row.
An optional per-category monthly limit (for example Menswear $100). A blank cap means unlimited. The ledger shows spent, cap, remaining, and over-budget state per category.
Current-month spend grouped by the wish's category, compared with the category caps.
Historical totals per month, used for the ledger's month-by-month view.
A convenience copy inside personal_context. It is recomputed from the ledger when gate state is normalized; editing it directly is temporary. The ledger is the source of truth.
personal_context.budget_month, the month key the cached spend belongs to.

A saved link that is useful as reference (learning, docs, business, tools, guides), not as a product being price-tracked. The Library is the subset of the Vault where librarySectionFor() returns a shelf; product links stay in the Vault's clusters.

One of 10 Library groupings: Education, Programming, AI/Data, Career, Business, Design, Cybersecurity, Utilities, Gaming, Sourcing. The API calls them sections; the UI calls them shelves and sections interchangeably.
The active Library count (1,017 in the seed). It excludes archived links. It is not the same as Signals indexed (1,346), which includes product links and non-library bookmarks.
A short note explaining the site. "What to use it for" (use_for) is the practical filing note. Both are editable per link.
The last health check:
UI label: LIVE Meaning: Checked and reachable.
UI label: BOT-BLOCKED Meaning: The site refused an automated request (403/challenge). Not proof the site is dead; kept for manual use.
UI label: NEEDS REVIEW Meaning: The check returned an unexpected error.
UI label: TIMEOUT Meaning: The check ran out of time.
UI label: DEAD Meaning: Confirmed unreachable. The audit removes confirmed-dead links, so this may appear only in older data.
UI label: UNCHECKED Meaning: No audit result yet.
UI label: Archived Meaning: Hidden from active counts and the default list; recoverable from the Archived filter.
The Library header's last-check summary from meta.library_audit: run time, checked count, live/blocked/error counts, removed count, and restored-after-review count.
A link the audit judged dead and deleted from the vault. The post-audit review restored false positives; data/library-removal-review.json records the decisions. Archived links are not removed links.

A normalized URL used to detect duplicates: lowercase host without www, no trailing slash, tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, etc.) stripped, remaining query parameters sorted. Meaningful parameters such as a docs version are preserved.
Two or more active Library links whose canonical URLs match. Extra copies is the number of links beyond the one you keep (group size − 1).
Keeps one link per canonical URL and marks the rest library_archived. Archived copies stay recoverable.
Select multiple links to Move them to another shelf, Archive them, or Restore archived links. Up to 250 at a time.

A different check: before promotion, the incoming title is compared with active wishes (token overlap ≥ 0.65 or an exact title match). It warns you before starting a second clock on the same product. It is not the same as a Library canonical-URL duplicate.
A cluster cover can be the generated reference illustration or a real wishlist photo. Product clusters prefer the exact item photo; reference-only clusters use the card.
A saved, structured playbook. "Protocol" is the data object; "routine" is the same thing in the UI. Protocols armed is the saved count (5 in the seed).
The ordered actions in a protocol. Up to 40 are stored, each up to 320 characters.
A free-text cadence such as "Daily — AM & PM" or "As needed". The parser infers it from AM/PM wording; you can edit it.
The protocol's grouping, usually "Skincare, Health & Protocols". It does not have to match a Vault cluster.
A short provenance label, for example "User-pasted — verify before use". It is not a trust score or a medical review.
Where the routine came from: TikTok, YouTube, a dermatologist, a product label, or a manual paste. Free text.
What source material was archived. Pasted routines usually say "Pasted text — source not archived"; it is not a claim that the video was downloaded.

Rules stores protocols. The hard constraints listed in You are separate: they are injected into Gate and oracle checks and shown as ENFORCED. A protocol guardrail is advice attached to that routine; it does not automatically block a purchase.
The safety note shown as ACTIVE GUARDRAIL. The parser detects four patterns:

Wishlist items attached to the protocol. Their photos, brands, and verified prices appear on the protocol card; clicking one opens the Gate. The routine builder searches the whole wishlist by name, brand, category and tag, and the picker shows 60 results at a time with a Show more button. Ticked products stay ticked while you filter, and Ticked only reviews the selection before saving. Up to 5 are auto-matched from the paste; up to 12 can be stored, and the picker refuses a 13th tick.
The Rules header card listing every protocol with a check-off for today's local date, a done/total score, and each protocol's current streak.

Marks a protocol done for one local calendar day. Unchecking removes that day. The log is stored per protocol in routine_log, capped at 400 days. The UI only offers today; the API rejects dates too far in the future.
Consecutive checked days ending today, or ending yesterday if today has not been checked yet. Missing a full day resets it to zero.

The deterministic paste parser: it detects AM/PM headers, numbered or bulleted steps, and semicolon-separated lists; infers a title, category, schedule, guardrail, and linked products. It does not require an API key. Paste limit: 12,000 characters.
Opens the same builder empty, for a manual protocol.
The personal_context object that every review, Gate check, and oracle prompt reads. It is the only source for the You panel.
UI label: Vault owner Meaning: Display name; initials are derived from the first two words.
UI label: under the name Meaning: Free-text location shown with "PERSONAL AI TRACK".
UI label: dossier grid Meaning: Key/value sizing notes (tops, bottoms, footwear, suits).
UI label: Hard constraints Meaning: The list labelled ENFORCED and passed into Gate/oracle reasoning.
UI label: Owned inventory Meaning: Items already owned, with brand, notes, and status; the basis of the Owned check.
UI label: Loved notes Meaning: Preferred scent notes.
UI label: Avoid Meaning: Notes to avoid.
UI label: Month cap Meaning: Same number as the Gate's monthly cap.
UI label: — Meaning: Derived from the ledger, not independently authoritative.
UI label: (no direct field) Meaning: Length applied to new gates; 14 in the seed. Existing wishes keep their own value.
UI label: — Meaning: The month key for the cached spend.
personal_context.owner. If missing, the UI falls back to "Vault Owner".

Free-text rules such as the Adapalene conflict, Halal requirement, aluminum-free deodorant, or caffeine cutoff. They are injected into gate and oracle prompts; they are not a medical device or a guarantee.
The closet/shelf list used by the Owned row on each wish. The seed tracks 6 items. "Already in rotation" is UI copy, not a separate table.
Loved and avoided fragrance notes, stored under fragrance_profile.

It changes future budget math immediately. It does not change the cooling period, the verdicts, or the inventory checks. To change the cooling period for new wishes, edit default_cooling_off_days; existing wishes keep their stored cooling_off_days.
The Capture action. Every ingest creates a bookmark; a wish is created only when the mode is screenshot, the classifier says wishlist, or a price is supplied.
URL (web/social link), Screenshot OCR (pasted OCR text from the camera roll), or Note (a life-hack/transcript). The mode changes the source labels and the model tier.

The dialog that shows the captured title, brand, cluster, retail price, expected price, source, and duplicate warning. Nothing is gated until you confirm. You can correct every field; a changed price is marked manual.
Turn a reviewed bookmark or pasted link into a wish and start its clock. The button reads Start 14-day gate.

A draggable bookmark that reads JSON-LD, OpenGraph, or a visible price in the open product tab, then opens /?capture= with the snapshot. It works on stores that block server-side fetches. The visible-price fallback is explicitly low confidence and prefers a sale price over a struck compare-at price.
The PWA registration that lets a phone share a product link into Stashov. It opens the same pre-gate review. HTTPS is required outside localhost.
The Gate's paste-a-link form with a clipboard Paste button. It skips the bookmark hunt and goes straight to review.
The state when a wish has no usable price. The card asks you to add details rather than inventing a number.
The OpenAI-compatible model API Stashov calls when NEBIUS_API_KEY is configured.
The deep-reasoning tier with a 1M-token context window; used for the oracle, impulse audits, and vault-wide synthesis.
The mid-tier model used for structuring work such as promotion and protocol generation.
The fast, cheap extraction tier used for classification and tagging.
The screenshot model that extracts product names, prices, and routine text from camera-roll text.
The local semantic-memory model that turns saved links and wishes into vectors for search and cross-linking.

Stashov sends each task to the cheapest tier that can do it: fast extraction (Nano), structuring/promotion (Super), deep reasoning (Ultra), vision OCR for screenshots, and embeddings for semantic memory. The UI calls this the model mesh.
The top-bar mode pill. NEBIUS LIVE means a usable API key is configured and calls go to Token Factory. DEMO FALLBACK means deterministic local traces are used instead; the app still works.

The deep-reasoning audit. Ask the oracle on a wish runs a one-item "talk me out of buying this" analysis; Ask across your entire vault runs a 1M-context synthesis over bookmarks, wishes, inventory, constraints, and routines.

Per-call rows with timestamp, task, model, tier, latency, input/output tokens, and estimated cost. The Router tab shows calls logged, tokens routed, average latency, estimated spend, the model mesh, and the most recent rows. Telemetry lives in its own small store, not in the 2.4 MB vault.

terms.term: Calls logged / Tokens routed / Avg latency / Router spend
terms.definition: The four Router stat cards. Calls counted from the recent telemetry window; tokens are input + output; latency is the mean of logged calls; spend is an estimate, not a billing statement.
keywords: Calls logged / Tokens routed / Avg latency / Router spend

terms.definition: The Nebius worker that verifies links, polls active wishes, counts newly cleared timers, finds deals, and writes the digest. Run serverless job triggers it on demand.
A wish whose retail-minus-floor saving is at least $20, surfaced in the digest. It is a price observation, not a purchase recommendation.
Downloads { app, version, exported_at, vault, sections, clusters } as JSON. It includes everything needed to restore, including the You profile.

Validates that the file has bookmark, wishlist, and protocol arrays, snapshots the current vault when local storage allows, normalizes gate state, and replaces the vault. Restoring replaces every room, including You. Export first.

A timestamped copy of the vault. Local installs keep .bak plus rotating snapshots in data/backups (last 20, at most one every 10 minutes). Hosted /tmp copies are ephemeral; the Blob object is the durable store.
Temp file → fsync → rename, so a crash cannot leave a half-written vault.
The default. Data lives in data/vault.json; the server binds to 127.0.0.1 unless configured otherwise.

Vercel with a private Blob store (BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN, or VERCEL=1 plus BLOB_STORE_ID). On first read, if state/vault.json is missing, the app seeds it from the bundled data/vault.json and writes it to Blob. After that, Blob is authoritative.
STASHOV_ACCESS_TOKEN gates the app and API. The unlock page exchanges the token for an HMAC-derived HttpOnly session cookie; the token is not stored in localStorage. Signed-out API calls return 401.
The installable web app. Its service worker intercepts the Web Share Target POST; it is not an offline cache. Vault data still needs the server.
